description.p: Sensor monitor for Debian, Ubuntu, Linux Mint and derivatives, on any desktop. Shows CPU, GPU, disks, fans and battery in the panel, in a window or floating on the desktop, with colors that change as temperatures rise and visual and sound alarms.

Monitor de sensores para Debian, Ubuntu, Linux Mint y derivadas, en cualquier escritorio. Muestra CPU, GPU, discos, ventiladores y batería en el panel, en una ventana o flotando en el escritorio, con colores que cambian al subir la temperatura y alarmas visuales y sonoras.
Alarms understand your processor: they know its design limit, warn when it slows down because of heat, when it gets hot while doing almost nothing or when a fan stops.
Las alarmas entienden tu procesador: conocen su límite de diseño y avisan si baja la velocidad por calor, si se calienta sin estar trabajando o si se para un ventilador.
It only reads sensors and never wakes up a sleeping dedicated graphics card.

description.p: Fixes the Cinnamon panel applet, which failed to load.

Gauges in the panel and up to 8 values, choosing which ones are shown in the bar and which only on click, names of your own for sensors, more alarm sounds (with a play button), disk intervals by disk type, Italian, German and Portuguese, and about ten times less CPU for the floating widget.

Fixes 42 bugs: readings and alarms no longer freeze when the system clock jumps, a hung notification daemon no longer blocks the service, and the window, panel and applets detect a frozen service reliably.

Reliability and security release: monitoring can no longer stop silently, damaged settings are never overwritten, alarms cannot be muted indefinitely by other programs, panels show "no data" when the service is not running, and the sensor detection helper is much more careful on laptops.
Works with Python 3.8 and 3.9, fixes a leak when the window is opened and closed, sensor order, Budgie detection and a floating widget that could not be unlocked.
Fixes a false critical alarm on Ryzen with an offset control temperature, alarms that never cleared and disk reads while scanning for sensors.
Sensor names in the panel; automatic restart after an upgrade.
Full AMD TjMax table from the official amd.com specifications (747 models), with priority over the per-family rules.

Fixes settings that were not saved, uninstalling, false critical alarms on Ryzen laptops and extra disk reads. New Cockpit and OLED styles, Bento window, exact CPU limits per AMD model, alarms by sustained throttling and a shared display logic for the panel, Cinnamon applet and desklet and the GNOME extension.
Smart alarms, 30-day history, sensor detection and GNOME extension.
